natural_language: Calls arrive at a helpdesk one at a time. The waiting time until the next call, in minutes, follows an exponential distribution whose MEAN waiting time is 4.0 minutes. Express the waiting-time model. Note that the exponential family in this language is parameterised by its rate, and rate equals one divided by the mean.
distractors: Passing 4.0 as the rate. This is the single commonest exponential-distribution error and it is invisible in prose, LaTeX and most code.
Declaring the waiting time over Real rather than PositiveReal, admitting negative waiting times.
Assuming 'rate' and 'lambda' are interchangeable without checking which convention the library uses (numpy takes a SCALE, scipy takes a scale, R takes a rate).
